```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The v4 nowcasts return a `csfmt_ensemble_v4`. The rate, trend, HLM and MEM
steps take one and return it with their results added. A full ensemble holds
draws in memory. A compressed ensemble holds a table with a point value and 9
percentiles for each base measure, and you store that table.

This vignette takes one simulated series from weekly counts to a stored table,
and back again.

## Build a full ensemble

The series has 320 weeks of positive tests out of all tests. Each week has 100
draws. Here they are simulated, but in a real run they come from a nowcast
such as `nowcast_ecdf_v4()`.

```{r build}
library(data.table)
library(csalert)

w <- cstime::dates_by_isoyearweek$isoyearweek
iyw <- w[match("2018-01", w) + 0:319]
season_week <- cstime::isoyearweek_to_seasonweek_n(iyw)
share <- 0.05 + 0.15 * exp(-(season_week - 25)^2 / 40)
set.seed(1)
tested <- matrix(rpois(320 * 100, 2000), nrow = 320)
positive <- matrix(rbinom(length(tested), tested, share), nrow = 320)

ens <- csfmt_ensemble_v4(
  data.table(location_code = "nation", isoyearweek = iyw),
  id_cols = "location_code",
  draws = list(positive = positive, tested = tested)
)
ens
```

Each draw matrix has one row per week and one column per draw. Column `j` is
the same draw in every measure.

## Add a rate, then run the trend and HLM

```{r steps}
ens <- ens_add_rate_v4(
  ens,
  numerator = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  per = 100,
  name = "positive_pr100"
)
ens <- short_term_trend_v4(
  ens,
  measure = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  name = "positive_pr100",
  seed = 4
)
ens <- signal_detection_hlm_v4(ens, measure = "positive_pr100")
ens$data[
  316:320,
  .(isoyearweek, positive_pr100_trend_pinc, positive_pr100_hlm_prob_high)
]
```

The trend models the counts of `positive` in a quasi-Poisson regression, with
the log of `tested` as the offset. `positive_pr100_trend_pinc` is
P(increasing). The HLM step compares each draw of the rate with a limit from
the 5 earlier years. `positive_pr100_hlm_prob_high` is the share of the draws
above that limit.

## Compress to a table

```{r compress}
stored <- ens_compress_v4(ens)
dim(stored)
max(nchar(names(stored), type = "bytes"))
```

The table holds the columns of `$data`. It also holds a median and 9
percentiles for each of the 3 base measures, `positive`, `tested` and
`positive_pr100`. It holds no draws, and each column is a plain vector.
`ens_compress_v4()` stops with an error when a name is longer than 63 bytes,
the limit of a PostgreSQL name. So you can write the table to PostgreSQL.

## Read the table back and run a step again

```{r rebuild}
back <- as_ensemble_v4(stored, id_cols = "location_code", n_sim = 100)
back
back <- short_term_trend_v4(
  back,
  measure = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  name = "positive_pr100",
  seed = 4
)
pinc <- data.table(
  isoyearweek = iyw,
  full = ens$data$positive_pr100_trend_pinc,
  rebuilt = back$data$positive_pr100_trend_pinc
)
pinc[316:320]
max(abs(pinc$full - pinc$rebuilt), na.rm = TRUE)
```

Each step rebuilds the draws of the base measures that it reads, from the
stored percentiles, with seed 4. `n_sim = 100` gives the same number of draws
as the full ensemble. The rebuild is an approximation. On this series, the two
P(increasing) values differ by at most 0.11 over the 318 weeks that have a
trend.

Each base measure gets its own u, so the rebuilt draws of `positive` and
`tested` are independent. The parts of a full ensemble from `nowcast_ecdf_v4()`
are independent too. A rate added again from its parts is their ratio.
Here `positive` depends on `tested`, so that ratio is too wide. Its median
interquartile range over the 320 weeks is 1.10 times that of the full rate. A
step on the stored rate rebuilds it from its own percentiles, at 1.01 times.
The chunk below adds the rate again from its parts.

```{r rate-again}
back <- ens_add_rate_v4(
  back,
  numerator = "positive",
  denominator = "tested",
  per = 100,
  name = "positive_pr100"
)
back <- signal_detection_hlm_v4(back, measure = "positive_pr100")
back
```
